what: The Truth Table Generator builds the complete truth table for any Boolean or logic expression, with a column for each step if you like. It understands AND, OR, NOT, XOR, NAND, NOR, implication (→) and biconditional (↔), written in words, symbols or programming style.

It also tells you whether the expression is a tautology, a contradiction or a contingency, lists minterms and maxterms, and gives a simplified sum-of-products formula. You can compare several expressions to check whether they are equivalent.
It is useful for discrete maths and logic courses, digital electronics and programmers checking conditions. It runs in your browser.
uses: Build tables for propositions such as (p → q) ∧ (q → r) → (p → r).
Type two expressions separated by a comma, such as De Morgan's laws, and see if they match.
Write expressions like A'B + AB' and get minterms and a simplified formula.
Check complex if-conditions written with && , || and !.
Show each intermediate column so students see how the result is built.
tutorial: Use letters for variables and any operator style: and, &, &&, ∧ or juxtaposition for AND; or, |, ||, ∨ or + for OR; not, !, ~, ¬ or a trailing ' for NOT. The symbol buttons insert ∧ ∨ ¬ ⊕ → ↔ ↑ ↓.
Each row is one combination of true and false values. The shaded column is the result; extra columns show each step when Show a column for each step is ticked.
See the number of true rows, whether the expression is always true, never true or sometimes true, and its minterms and maxterms.
The sum of products is minimised with the Quine–McCluskey method, for up to 10 variables. Choose logic, digital or code notation.
Separate up to six expressions with commas. The tool says whether they are equivalent.
Show 1/0 or T/F, start with all false or all true, then copy the table as CSV or Markdown, or copy the simplified formula.
features: Words, maths symbols, programming symbols and digital notation, including NAND, NOR and XNOR.
Σm and ΠM lists and the canonical sum of products.
Quine–McCluskey minimisation with an exact cover for small cases.
Tables of up to 4,096 rows, copyable as CSV or Markdown.

example.title: Worked example: majority of three
example.text: Type ABC + AB'C + A'BC. The table has 8 rows and the result is true in rows 3, 5 and 7, so the minterms are Σm(3, 5, 7). In digital notation the simplified formula is BC + AC: the output is 1 when C is 1 and at least one of A or B is 1.

tips: Implication p → q is false only when p is true and q is false.
Without the long-names option, AB means A AND B. Tick Long variable names to use words like rain and wind as variables.
NOT binds tightest, then AND, XOR, OR, implication and biconditional. Use brackets when in doubt.
T and F are treated as variables. Use 1/0 or true/false for constants.
problems: An operator has nothing on one side, as in A and. Complete the expression.
Up to 12 variables are supported, which already gives 4,096 rows.
It is shown for up to 10 variables; larger expressions still get the table and minterm list.
